newsitem.title: USA: U.S. spot gas prices hold modest gains on storage.
newsitem.headline: U.S. spot gas prices hold modest gains on storage.

text.p: U.S. spot natgas prices held modest gains again Tuesday, as steady storage buying helped offset tapering demand from mild U.S. weather, traders said.

And despite forecasts for more below-normal temperatures next week, traders said low stocks, particularly in the producing region, and favorable autumn-to-winter price spreads could mean more support for physical prices near-term.

"There's still a need to get gas in the ground in the producing region and that could give some support to the market," said one trader. U.S. Gulf Coast swing prices were steady to up slightly this morning to the $1.85-1.90 area.
Gulf cash prices are now about 10 cents over index, and another trader expected them to stay that way for a while.
"There's still a lot of demand for storage, and with more than a full carry in the market, you buy it," said a Houston-based trader.
Midcontinent prices firmed more than five cents on the day to the mid-$1.70s, also almost a dime over September indices.
In west Texas, El Paso Permian gained a few cents to the mid-$1.60s, now slightly over Sept 1 levels. South Texas was up slightly to the low-$1.80s, more than five cents over index.
In the Northeast, gas at the New York city gate was up several cents to near the $2.10 area.
